definitions.explanation: A large semiaquatic mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa, known for spending much of its time in rivers and lakes.

examples.english: Hippos spend much of their time in the water.

examples.japanese: ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{河馬|かば}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けて→開ける：00563_akeru⟧⟦いました→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The hippo was opening its large mouth at the zoo.

examples.japanese: {河馬|かば}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{見|み}た{目|め}→見た目：14110_mitame⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Hippos are more dangerous animals than they appear.

{河馬|かば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{生|う}まれて→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧、⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: A baby hippo was born at the zoo and became a big topic of conversation.

notes:
WRITING:
- The kanji {河馬|かば} is rare in everyday text. Animal names are normally written in katakana, so カバ is the usual form; かば also appears.
- The name is literally "river horse" (⟦{河|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧ = river, ⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧ = horse), matching the Greek origin of "hippopotamus."

COUNTING PATTERNS:
- Counted with ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧, the counter for large animals: {一頭|いっとう}, {二頭|にとう}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{河馬|かば} (the hippo at the zoo) — where learners most often meet the word
- {河馬|かば}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (the hippo opens its huge mouth)

USAGE:
- Despite its placid image, {河馬|かば} is often described in Japanese as ⟦{見|み}た{目|め}→見た目：14110_mitame⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧ (more dangerous than it looks), a phrase worth knowing in its own right.
